gallery.title: File:Reading Room of the Boston Public Library.jpg
gallery.source: Reading Room of the Boston Public Library
gallery.description: Reading-Room of the Boston Public Library, an engraving drawn by J. J. Harley and printed January 1871 in Every Saturday, a weekly newspaper published in Boston by James Osgood & Company. This depicts the library's first Boylston Street building, which was designed by architect Charles Kirk Kirby (1826-1910). Used between 1858 and 1895, it was replaced by the present building on Copley Square.

gallery.filename: Bookplate (Exlibris) "The Trustees of the Public Library of the City of Boston 1852 -1878" "The Paul Sabatier Franciscan Collection" (cropped).jpg
gallery.title: File:Bookplate (Exlibris) "The Trustees of the Public Library of the City of Boston 1852 -1878" "The Paul Sabatier Franciscan Collection" (cropped).jpg
gallery.artist: Jacopone, da Todi, 1230-1306; Sabatier, Paul, 1858-1928; Ludwig Rosenthal's Antiquariat
gallery.description: Ms. codex.; Bibliographic record created by BPL staff based on description by Dr. Lisa Fagin Davis.; Origin: Written in Northern Italy in the late fifteenth century; some orthographic features, in particular the use of [-xia] for [-sia] at the end of a word, suggest a possible origin in Venice.; Bond, W.H. Supplement to the Census of medieval and Renaissance manuscripts in the United States and Canada, 925; Immediate source of acquisition: Acquired by the BPL from Sabatier's estate in 1930 along with several other manuscripts and his library of Francisciana, collectively known as the "Paul Sabatier Franciscan Collection" (Schoenberg Database of Manuscripts 42807 and 198008). BPL plate inside front cover.; Bibliography: Zoltan Haraszti, "An Early Franciscan Breviary," More Books VII (1931): 327-340; Zoltan Haraszti, "A Library about St. Francis," More Books VII (1931): 275; L. Leonardo and G. Marrani, LIO - ITS/ Repertorio della Lirica Italiana delle Origini (Florence, 2005).; In Latin and Italian.; Provenance: Early modern pencil notations inside front cover and on first flyleaf, #1014 on front cover and inner front pastedown. Sold by Ludwig Rosenthal to Franciscan scholar and biographer Paul Sabatier (1858-1928).; A compilation of miscellaneous contents, in Latin and Italian. Fol. 69-130v comprises hymns and poems, many of which are by Franciscan poet Jacopone da Todi (d. 1306). This section is misbound; the correct order, with reference current folio numbers, should be as follows: 101-130, [14 leaves lacking], 93-100, 85-92, 69-84. In the contents list for this bibliographic record, the original foliation number is given in brackets, with the incipits of the missing 14 leaves supplied from the16th-century index on fol. 46-47v. When possible, reference is given to corresponding entry in LIO, i.e., L. Leonardo and G. Marrani, Repertorio della Lirica Italiana delle Origini (Florence, 2005).
